title: Unit 2 Stand-alone 7: Prioritization - New Back Pain in Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm

question.stem: The nurse should first assess the client
question.preamble: The nurse has received information about assigned clients.

options.text: with multiple sclerosis (MS) who had an indwelling urethral catheter removed 5 hours ago and has not been able to urinate
with an abdominal aortic aneurysm who reports recent onset of low back pain
who had coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery 2 days ago and reports sternal pain when coughing
who has bacterial pneumonia and is requesting a cough suppressant

question.explanation: New onset low back pain in a client with a known abdominal aortic aneurysm (Option 2) is a classic warning sign of aneurysm expansion or impending rupture, a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate assessment. Urinary retention after recent catheter removal in a client with MS (Option 1) needs assessment but is not immediately life-threatening. Sternal pain with coughing 2 days after CABG surgery (Option 3) is an expected postoperative finding. A request for a cough suppressant in a client with bacterial pneumonia (Option 4) is a reasonable, non-urgent request.
